Andrej kissed him with the starvation of a man who has been denied food for a lifetime, his teeth clashing against Rimmon’s, his tongue tasting the inside of his mouth like he was trying to memorize the shape of it.
Rimmon’s hands flew up, tangling in Andrej’s hair, pulling him closer, though they were already pressed so tight it was hard to tell where one body ended and the other began. He groaned into the kiss, a sound of pure relief, of a hunger finally, finally met.
Andrej’s hands were everywhere. They were rough, calloused sandpaper against Rimmon’s skin, snagging on the fabric of his tunic. He gripped Rimmon’s waist, then slid up to his neck, his thumbs pressing into the pulse point there.
"Rimmon," he gasped, breaking the kiss to bury his face in the crook of Rimmon’s neck. He inhaled sharply, a shuddering breath that racked his entire frame. "Gods. Rimmon."
"I'm here," Rimmon whispered, his cheek resting on the top of Andrej’s head. The hair was soft, smelling of smoke and the desert wind. "I'm right here."
"Come," Andrej said against his skin.
He grabbed Rimmon’s hand, his grip crushing, and pulled him deeper into the tannery. They navigated the obstacle course of drying racks and vats by instinct and the faint, milky light of the moon filtering through the high slats of the roof.
They reached the back, where the piles of finished hides lay stacked—soft goat skins, not yet dyed, smelling of sumac and earth. Andrej didn't bother with a bed. He pulled a heavy stack of skins down onto the packed earth floor, creating a chaotic, soft nest in the shadows.
He turned to Rimmon, his chest heaving. The moonlight sliced across his face, illuminating the sharp cheekbones, the hollows of his eyes, the wet shine of his lips. He looked wild. He looked beautiful.
"No more words," Andrej commanded, his voice rough. "I am done with words."
He reached out and took hold of the hem of Rimmon’s tunic.
Rimmon lifted his arms, the fabric sliding up, over his head, and away. The night air was cool on his skin, but Andrej’s gaze was hot enough to burn. Andrej stripped off his own tunic with frantic, jerky movements, tossing it aside into the darkness.
Skin to skin.
The contact was a shock, a revelation. When Andrej pulled him down onto the pile of skins, the sensation was overwhelming—the softness of the leather beneath, the hardness of Andrej’s body above.
There was no finesse. There was no practiced seduction. It was a grappling, a wrestling match of limbs and lips. Rimmon ran his hands down the long, smooth line of Andrej’s back, feeling the muscles bunch and shift, tracing the scars of the tannery work—the small burns, the scrapes—mapping the history of the man he loved.
Andrej was fervent, his hands exploring Rimmon with a kind of desperate reverence. He touched Rimmon’s face, his chest, his stomach, as if trying to verify that he was real, that he wasn't a mirage born of heat and loneliness.
"Mine," Andrej muttered, the word vibrating against Rimmon’s collarbone. "For this hour. Mine."
"Yours," Rimmon gasped, arching into the touch, his eyes fluttering shut. "Always yours."
The world narrowed down to sensation. The smell of the hides. The grit of the floor. The friction of their bodies. The sounds of their breathing, harsh and ragged in the quiet workshop.
Every touch was a protest against the future, a defiance of the letter written in elegant script, a rebellion against the date set in two moons. Rimmon gave himself over to it completely, burning the memory of Andrej’s weight, the texture of his hair, the taste of him, into every fiber of his being. He wanted to be scarred by this. He wanted to carry the mark of it under his wedding robes, a secret burn that would never heal.
When the end came, it was a shattering. It left them both gasping, tangled together on the heap of skins, slick with sweat, the chill finally seeping into their bones.
Silence returned to the tannery, but it was different now. It was no longer empty. It was filled with the heavy, sated weight of the truth.
Rimmon lay on his back, staring up at the slivers of moonlight in the roof. Andrej was heavy on his chest, his face buried in the curve of Rimmon’s neck, his breathing slowly evening out. Rimmon brought his hand up, his fingers drifting idly through Andrej’s hair, tracing the shape of his ear.
He felt a wetness on his skin.
He froze. Andrej was crying. Silent, still, hot tears that soaked into the hollow of Rimmon’s throat.
Rimmon’s heart broke, quietly and irreparably. He didn't speak. He didn't offer empty comforts. There was no comfort for this. This was the funeral feast, just as the bachelor vigil had promised. They had tasted the wine, and it was sweeter than anything in the world, and now the cup was empty.
He simply wrapped his arms tighter around Andrej’s shoulders, holding him against the inevitable dawn, wishing he could stop the turning of the earth, wishing he could freeze the stars in the sky and live forever in the scent of cured leather and the salt of Andrej’s tears.
The dawn did not come with hope. It came like a thief, stealing the sanctuary of the dark and replacing it with the flat, grey honesty of morning.
